passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We operate in a business environment that involves significant risks, many of which are beyond the Registrants’ control. The Registrants regularly evaluate the most significant risks of their businesses and review those risks with their respective boards of directors and, if appropriate, committees of those boards of directors. The following risk factors and all other information contained in this report should be considered carefully when evaluating the Registrants, and unless a risk factor expressly excludes a Registrant or the context requires otherwise, references to “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to both Registrants. These risk factors could affect our financial results and cause such results to differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements made by or on behalf of us. Below, we have identified risks we consider material. The risks that we face are not limited to those in this section. There may be additional risks and uncertainties (either currently unknown or not currently believed to be material) that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, liquidity or cash flows. Although the risks are organized by headings, and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. These risk factors should be read in conjunction with Item 1., "Business,” Item 7., "Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” and in other sections of this Form 10-K that include forward-looking and other statements involving risks and uncertainties that could impact our business, financial condition, results of operations, liquidity or cash flows. Risks Associated with Damage to Our Reputation and Securities Class-Action Litigation Securities class-action litigation against us could have a material adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations, our ability to access capital, liquidity or cash flows. On July 21, 2021, FE entered into a three-year DPA with the U.S. Attorney’s Office that, subject to court proceedings, resolves the previously disclosed U.S. Attorney’s Office investigation into us relating to our lobbying and governmental affairs activities concerning HB 6. Under the DPA, we paid a $230 million monetary penalty in 2021 and agreed to the filing of a criminal information charging FirstEnergy with one count of conspiracy to commit honest services wire fraud. As of July 22, 2024, we successfully completed the obligations required within the three-year term of the DPA. Under the DPA, and until the conclusion of any related investigation, criminal prosecution and civil proceeding brought by the U.S. Attorney’s Office, we have an obligation to continue (i) publishing quarterly a list of all payments to 501(c)(4) entities and all payments to entities known by us to be operating for the benefit of a public official, either directly or indirectly; (ii) not making any statements that contradict the DPA; (iii) notifying the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the S.D. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers the dividend more than threefold, so common distributions are funded from internally generated cash rather than incremental borrowing, a meaningful support for the equity cushion beneath the debt stack.
Operating cash flow relative to debt improved year over year and sits close to the utilities sector median, indicating that cash generation has strengthened even as the capital programme expanded.

key_risks.text: Leverage is elevated and deteriorating: gross leverage rose versus the prior year and stands well above the sector median, placing the issuer in the weakest percentile band for both gross and net leverage among electric utilities.

Disclosed risks include government investigations and securities class-action litigation tied to the deferred prosecution agreement, which could impair reputation, capital access and liquidity, and regulatory or severe-weather outcomes could raise storm restoration costs materially.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage fell year over year and is below the sector median, while EBITDA coverage of interest also trails peers; the EBITDA proxy excludes intangible amortization, so true coverage may be modestly better than reported.

Free cash flow is negative because capital expenditure exceeds operating cash flow, and the current ratio is below one and below the sector median, so near-term maturities and the capital programme depend on continued market access.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged, with leverage above the sector median and cash-flow-to-debt coverage only mid-pack; the upgrade path requires meaningful EBITDA growth or debt reduction, which we view as unlikely near term.

Our judgement is a stable but constrained credit trajectory: regulated electric cash flows are predictable, yet negative free cash flow, thin liquidity and heavy capital spending leave refinancing reliant on capital markets, and the debt maturity ladder concentrates repayments in the middle years.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流覆蓋股息超過三倍，因此普通股分派乃由內部產生之現金而非增量借貸提供資金，對債務層之下的股本緩衝構成有意義的支持。
營運現金流相對債務較上年改善，並接近公用事業行業中位數，顯示即使資本計劃擴大，現金產生能力亦有所增強。

key_risks.text: 槓桿偏高且正在惡化：總槓桿較上年上升，並遠高於行業中位數，使發行人於電力公用事業中，總槓桿及淨槓桿均處於最弱百分位區間。
已披露風險包括與延遲起訴協議相關的政府調查及證券集體訴訟，可能損害聲譽、資本市場准入及流動性，而監管或惡劣天氣結果可能大幅提高風暴復原成本。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率較上年下降，並低於行業中位數，而EBITDA對利息之覆蓋亦落後同業；EBITDA代理指標不包括無形資產攤銷，故真實覆蓋可能略優於報告數字。
自由現金流為負，因資本開支超過營運現金流，而流動比率低於一且低於行業中位數，故短期到期債務及資本計劃依賴持續的市場准入。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為高度槓桿，槓桿高於行業中位數，而現金流對債務之覆蓋僅屬中游；升級路徑需要有意義的EBITDA增長或債務減少，我們認為短期內不太可能。
我們的判斷為穩定但受限的信用軌跡：受監管電力現金流可預測，然而負自由現金流、流動性薄弱及沉重資本開支使再融資依賴資本市場，而債務到期階梯將還款集中於中期年份。
